entries.title: Angelic Defense Blessings — Evidence-Backed Choir
entries.summary: Quilla's ten angelic blessings name real defense bundles against unauthorized pentest tooling, Trojans, overlays, and sideload droppers — never supernatural wards.
entries.body: Each Sephirot angel labels a concrete CoreGuard surface: Metatron (debugger/signature crown), Raziel (intel sync), Tzaphkiel (codex teaching), Tzadkiel (Nemesis scan), Kamael (Privacy Shield), Raphael (priority correlation), Haniel (consentful actions), Michael (Frida/hooks/root swarm), Gabriel (timeline/telemetry memory), Sandalphon (overlay/Accessibility/sideload kingdom). Blessings are ACTIVE/WATCHING/BREACHED/IDLE only from Guardian Score checks and Memory. They do not invent hits. Against unauthorized red-team instrumentation and intrusive Trojans, the choir raises human attention — you still run Scanner, arm Shield with VPN consent, and revoke abusive overlays.
entries.defense: Ask Quilla for a priority status brief or "angelic defense blessings". On BREACHED Michael/Sandalphon lines, stop sensitive work, revoke overlays/Accessibility you do not trust, re-scan with Nemesis, and arm Shield.

entries.title: Defense Against Unauthorized Instrumentation (Frida / Red-Team Tooling)
entries.summary: Michael's blessing maps to Frida, hook maps, memory integrity, mount integrity, and root checks — plus the on-device swarm.
entries.body: Unauthorized dynamic instrumentation (Frida, Xposed-style hooks, memory patches) is a common red-team and malware technique. CoreGuard answers with native ptrace anti-debug, text-segment baselines, Frida port/thread heuristics, hook library map scans, and swarm agents that hand off CRITICAL signals. This is defensive RASP for your device — not a license to attack others. Authorized pentests require rules of engagement; Quilla refuses unauthorized attack how-tos.
entries.defense: If Frida/hook checks FAIL: treat the runtime as hostile, end sensitive sessions, reinstall from Play if integrity is doubted, and re-run Guardian Score.

entries.title: Defense Against Intrusive Trojans (Overlay · Accessibility · Sideload)
entries.summary: Sandalphon's kingdom blessing watches overlay holders, third-party Accessibility services, and sideload risk — classic Trojan delivery and capture paths.
entries.body: Intrusive Android Trojans often combine: (1) sideloaded APK droppers outside Play, (2) SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW overlays that fake bank/login UI, and (3) Accessibility services that capture input or drive the UI. CoreGuard's Sandalphon checks inventory these surfaces and Quilla teaches overlay phishing / sideload dropper topics. Pair with Tzadkiel (Nemesis IOC scan) and Kamael (DNS Shield) for depth.
entries.defense: Revoke draw-over-apps and Accessibility for apps you do not fully trust. Prefer Play installs. Run Nemesis after any unexpected APK. Arm Privacy Shield with VPN consent.
